title: Isolation and lock-off procedure
summary: Sets out the safe isolation, lock-off and proving dead procedure for single and three phase supplies, using GS38-compliant test equipment, plus re-energising and multi-person lock-off.

sections.heading: Isolation, lock-off and testing
paragraphs: Before working on electrical installations or circuits you must identify the circuit(s) you will work on and use the correct means of isolation, so the supply cannot be reinstated while you work. The isolation method must always be under the control of the person doing the work.
In addition to isolation, the circuit must be tested to prove that it is dead, using an approved test method.
bullets: Identify the circuit before isolating
Isolation must be under the control of the person doing the work
Prove dead using an approved test method

sections.heading: Means of isolation
paragraphs: Depending on whether you are working on a circuit or an individual piece of equipment, any of the listed means may be used, provided it is always under your control. It must not be possible for another person to re-energise the circuit.

Modern buildings often have secondary sources of supply, such as UPS units, solar PV supplies or stand-by generators. When isolating the main source you must ensure all other sources of energy are also isolated.
bullets: Circuit breaker at distribution board/consumer unit
Fuse removal at distribution board/consumer unit
Disconnection of plug and socket
Fuse removal at spur connection outlet
Switch disconnection

sections.heading: Locking off in practice
paragraphs: With a circuit breaker at the DB/CU, switch the device off and lock it with a suitable locking-off clip and a padlock that opens only with a unique key or combination. The key or combination must stay with the person doing the work.
With a re-wireable fuse, remove the fuse and fit a suitable locking device so a substitute fuse cannot be fitted. The original fuse must be kept in your possession at all times.
bullets: Plug and socket: used when working on equipment; make sure the plug cannot be re-inserted; if in doubt, remove the plug
Spur connection unit: remove the fuse, keep it in your possession and fit a locking device to the fuse carrier
It is not acceptable to isolate equipment using the switch on the spur outlet
Fuse removal only isolates one of the line conductors, so test to prove dead afterwards
Switch: only acceptable if you can ensure it cannot be operated; it may be faulty and isolate only one line conductor, so test afterwards

sections.heading: GS38 test equipment
paragraphs: Guidance Note GS38: Electrical test equipment for use on low voltage electrical systems is an HSE document. It gives guidelines for those testing electrical circuits on the safety requirements for test instruments and leads, and on methods of ensuring circuits are dead.

GS38 advocates an approved voltage test instrument with a suitable means of proving that the instrument is itself functioning correctly. Voltage indicators for testing 230 V and 400 V supplies come with a proving unit.
bullets: Before use, visually check the voltage indicator and proving unit for cracked casing
Check for damaged insulation (abrasion, cuts or perishing of flexible insulation)
Check for loose terminals

sections.heading: Safe isolation procedure
paragraphs: Follow the procedure in order, using the voltage indicator and proving unit. The instrument is proved before and after the test to make sure it worked throughout.
bullets: Locate and confirm the supply to be isolated; tell the customer of possible implications where necessary
Fit a locking device to the isolation device
Fit a warning notice to the point of isolation
Test the voltage indicator using the proving unit
Confirm all conductors are dead: between all Lines and Neutral, all Lines and Earth, and Neutral and Earth
Re-test the voltage indicator using the proving unit

sections.heading: Proving dead: single and three phase
paragraphs: On a single phase supply, prove the indicator on the proving unit, then test between all terminals; there should be no voltage indication between any of them. Prove the indicator again afterwards.
On a three phase supply the same method is used with a set order of tests, again proving the indicator before and after.
bullets: Three phase test order: first between each Phase
Second, between each Phase and Neutral
Third, between each Phase and CPC
Finally, between Neutral and CPC
Use the proving unit before and after testing

sections.heading: Re-energising and multi-person lock-off
paragraphs: After completing the work and the required inspection and testing, remove the lock-off devices, locks and labels and restore the electrical supply.

Where more than one person works on an installation or circuit, a multi-key lock-off device must be used and each person attaches their own lock. No one can re-energise the circuit until all persons have removed their locks, showing their part of the work is finished.
bullets: Re-energise only after inspection and testing are complete
Remove lock-off devices, locks and labels
Multi-key lock-off: each worker fits their own lock

flashcards.front: What must you do before working on a circuit, apart from isolating it?
flashcards.back: Test it to prove that it is dead, using an approved test method.

flashcards.front: Who must control the isolation method?
flashcards.back: The person undertaking the work. It must not be possible for another person to re-energise the circuit.

flashcards.front: List the accepted means of isolation.
flashcards.back: Circuit breaker at DB/CU, fuse removal at DB/CU, disconnecting a plug and socket, fuse removal at a spur connection outlet, and switch disconnection.

flashcards.front: What must you remember about secondary supplies when isolating?
flashcards.back: Modern buildings may have UPS units, solar PV or stand-by generators. When isolating the main source, all other sources of energy must also be isolated.

flashcards.front: How do you lock off a circuit breaker?
flashcards.back: Switch it off and lock it with a locking-off clip and a padlock opened only by a unique key or combination, which you retain.

flashcards.front: How do you isolate using a re-wireable fuse?
flashcards.back: Remove the fuse, fit a suitable locking device so a substitute can't be fitted, and keep the original fuse in your possession.

flashcards.front: Is using the switch on a spur outlet acceptable for isolation?
flashcards.back: No. Isolate by removing the fuse, keeping it, and locking the fuse carrier.

flashcards.front: Why must you test after isolating by fuse removal or switch?
flashcards.back: Fuse removal only isolates one of the line conductors, and a switch may be faulty and isolate only one line conductor.
HSE Guidance Note on electrical test equipment for use on low voltage electrical systems: safety requirements for test instruments and leads, and methods for ensuring circuits are dead.

flashcards.front: What should you check on a voltage indicator before use?
flashcards.back: Cracked casing, damaged insulation (abrasion, cuts or perishing of flexible insulation) and loose terminals.

flashcards.front: When is the voltage indicator checked on the proving unit?
flashcards.back: Before testing the circuit and again after testing, to confirm it still works.

flashcards.front: In what order are three phase tests made?
flashcards.back: Between each Phase, then each Phase and Neutral, then each Phase and CPC, and finally Neutral and CPC.
After the work and the required inspection and testing, remove lock-off devices, locks and labels, then restore the supply.

flashcards.front: Why use a multi-key lock-off when several people work on a circuit?
flashcards.back: Each person attaches their own lock, so nobody can re-energise until all have removed their locks.

quiz.q: Who must keep control of the isolation method while you work on a circuit?
quiz.why: The isolation method must at all times be under the control of the person undertaking the work.

quiz.q: When isolating the main supply of a modern building, what else must you do?
options: Nothing; only the main supply matters
Isolate any other energy sources such as UPS, solar PV or stand-by generators
Ask the client to switch them off later
quiz.why: When isolating the main source, all other sources of energy must also be isolated.

quiz.q: How should a circuit breaker at a DB/CU be locked off?
options: With a clip and a padlock opened only by a unique key or combination, retained by the person doing the work
With a padlock whose key hangs on the board
quiz.why: Use an appropriate locking-off clip with a padlock that has a unique key or combination which you keep.

quiz.q: After removing a fuse to isolate a circuit, what should you do with it?
options: Keep it in your possession at all times
Put it in your toolbox without a lock-off device
quiz.why: The original fuse must be kept in your possession at all times, and a locking device fitted to prevent a substitute.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT an acceptable way to isolate equipment on a spur?
options: Removing the fuse and locking the carrier
Using the switch on the spur outlet
quiz.why: It is not acceptable to isolate equipment using the switch on the spur outlet.

quiz.q: Why must a circuit still be tested dead after fuse removal?
options: Fuse removal only isolates one of the line conductors
quiz.why: Fuse removal only isolates one of the line conductors, so testing is needed to prove it is dead.

quiz.q: Which document gives HSE guidance on electrical test equipment for low voltage systems?
quiz.why: Guidance Note GS38 covers requirements for test instruments and leads and for ensuring circuits are dead.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a proving unit?
options: To prove the voltage indicator is functioning correctly
quiz.why: GS38 advocates a voltage test instrument with a means of proving the instrument itself is working.

quiz.q: Which fault would mean a voltage indicator is unsafe to use?
quiz.why: Visual checks look for cracked casing, damaged insulation and loose terminals.

quiz.q: Which sequence is correct for the isolation procedure?
options: Test dead, fit lock, fit notice, prove indicator
Prove the indicator, test, fit lock, fit notice
Fit lock, fit notice, prove indicator, test all conductors, re-prove indicator
Fit notice, remove lock, test once
quiz.why: Lock off, fit a warning notice, prove the indicator, test all conductors, then re-test the indicator on the proving unit.

quiz.q: On a three phase supply, which test comes last?
quiz.why: The order is Phase to Phase, Phase to Neutral, Phase to CPC, and finally Neutral to CPC.

quiz.q: Several people work on one installation. What must be used?
options: A multi-key lock-off device with each person attaching their own lock
quiz.why: Each person attaches their own lock, so no one can re-energise until all locks are removed.
